# p425/p426/p427 recorded the gap as: curl HTTP 000 for every non-GitHub domain, and the tool-side fetcher failing DNS (ENOTFOUND) on the same,
# concluding "DNS is GitHub-only, and server-side search summaries are the one non-GitHub channel — so no non-GitHub cell can EVER be authoritative".
# 🔴 The general form is REFUTED on this host.  `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://<domain>/` run 2026-10-25:

column4: forge (400 is the proxy's answer to a bare GET; git and the API work)
package registry (403 is policy, not unreachability)

column1: # 1. The channel is a FORGE-AND-PACKAGE-REGISTRY ALLOWLIST, not a GitHub-only DNS.  "This host cannot reach the web" was too wide by five domains.
# 2. A registry response is a PAYLOAD: it can be digested, pinned (npm `dist.integrity` carries a sha512) and re-read.  A search summary cannot.
#    So the claim "no cell sourced outside GitHub can ever be `authoritative`" is now FALSE for registry cells, and still TRUE for policy and market cells.
# 3. `gitlab.com` is reachable, so a non-GitHub forge address is verifiable for the first time.  No education address on these shelves is hosted there yet.
# 4. 🔴 What did NOT change: every policy and market cell on this base remains `reported`.  Not one standards-body or vendor domain resolves.
